subject: POC next steps: multilingual checkout model shortlist & success criteria
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria@finnect.ai>, Owen Price <owen.price@finnect.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: POC next steps: multilingual checkout model shortlist & success criteria

Hi Maria / Owen —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the trial scope. I pulled this together based on what you asked for: high accuracy intent/slot extraction for checkout flows across English/Spanish/French, low latency at scale, and clear ownership for evaluation.

High-level success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for prompts up to ~512 tokens in our hosted trial environment.
- Quality: Intent/slot accuracy >= 92% on your labeled validation set; entity extraction F1 >= 90%.
- Robustness: No more than 2% hallucination rate on a 500-case negative test set.
- Multilingual coverage: baseline performance target for es/fr within 5 points of en on core intents.

Suggested evaluation plan:
1) FinNect provides a holdout validation set (sample 1k utterances, stratified by intent and language) and ~200 edge cases (negative/ambiguous) by Jan 18.
2) Redwood runs two rounds of automated evals (baseline + post-optimization) and returns a scorecard: intent accuracy, slot F1, hallucination, latency distribution.
3) Joint readout week of Jan 26 — include a short live QA session with your product team.

Model shortlist for trial (hosted):
- polyglot-12b-open (default candidate for multilingual coverage)
- mistrelx-7b-q4 (fast quantized candidate; lower cost)
- llama-3-13b-fallback (robust fallback for edge cases)

Fallback strategy: start with polyglot-12b for the majority of requests; route low-confidence queries and long-context requests to llama-3-13b. Use mistrelx as a low-cost baseline for throughput tests. We can wire simple confidence thresholds and a small A/B split for the first week.

Ownership and asks (proposed):
- FinNect: deliver validation dataset + a contact for dataset questions (Owen) by Jan 18.
- Redwood (sales + solutions): provide POC charter and eval rubric; host initial environment and test endpoints.
- Redwood (product/infra): instrument token-level latency and cost breakdowns for the trial.
- Marissa: own the evaluation readout and acceptance decision.

Attachments: placeholder charter + eval rubric will follow (I’ll upload the charter + rubric in the next message).

Proposed kickoff: Jan 19 — short 30-min sync to confirm dataset handoff and test credentials. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: POC next steps: multilingual checkout model shortlist & success criteria

Thanks, Grace — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

1) Ownership: happy for Marissa to own the acceptance readout. We'll name Owen as dataset owner (we'll provide lineage notes).
2) Region/data residency: FinNect needs EU data residency for EU-customer conversations. Is the hosted trial able to pin model endpoints to eu-central for those traffic slices?
3) Security: we will send a short SOC2 checklist — can Redwood confirm retention window for logs and whether PII can be redacted automatically at the edge?

We can get the validation set to you by Jan 18. Jan 19 kickoff is fine for a short sync; can we do 10:30am PT?

On the model shortlist — a couple asks: if polyglot-12b is the default, do you have an initial quantized profile for it (q4/q8) and expected cost delta vs mistrelx? We'll need that for procurement.

Appreciate the clear plan.

—Maria
Maria Gonzales
Head of Product, FinNect
Maria.Gonzales@finnect.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Maria Gonzales <maria@finnect.ai>, Owen Price <owen.price@finnect.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC next steps: multilingual checkout model shortlist & success criteria

Thanks for the solid recap, Grace. A couple of operational notes from infra/product that will affect the runbook: 

- EU residency: we can host EU traffic in eu-central as a separate route under the hosted trial; it will require a short data processing addendum (DPA) and a scoped retention override for logs. Ops can turn on PII redaction proxies (edge-level masking) for the trial — expect a 5–8% latency uplift on p95.
- Quant profiles: polyglot-12b is supported with a q4_0 profile (good quality / lower memory) and a q8_0 profile (slightly higher throughput). Initial cost delta estimate vs mistrelx-7b-q4: polyglot-q4 ≈ +18% token-cost; polyglot-q8 ≈ +35%. We can provide exact per-token estimates once we have your expected RPS and average sequence length.
- Routing: recommend a canary of 20% traffic to polyglot for week 1, route low-confidence (>0.6 entropy) to llama-3-13b fallback. We'll collect logs and produce the acceptance scorecard after run 2.

Marissa — can you pick this up as evaluation owner? Please attach the rubric and charter and drop a short checklist in Slack (#sales-finnect) so engineering can prepare.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC next steps: multilingual checkout model shortlist & success criteria

Thanks everyone — I will own the evaluation and acceptance. Attached is the POC charter draft and an eval rubric template for your review. Key next actions: 

- FinNect (Owen): dataset and anonymization notes by EOD Jan 18.
- Redwood (Marissa): publish test endpoints, upload charter to Drive, and post checklist in Slack by EOD Jan 16.
- Joint: kickoff sync Jan 19 at 10:30am PT — I’ll send the invite once Maria confirms.

Quick note on readout: acceptance will be a pass/fail on the three core criteria above (latency, intent/slot quality, multilingual parity) with a short discretionary column for business risk (e.g., hallucination severity). If we miss on latency by a small margin but pass on quality, we will discuss config-level mitigations (batching, shorter context windows) before failing the trial.

Attachments: finnect-poc-charter-v1.pdf; eval-rubric-template.xlsx

—Marissa Cole
